title: NonStationaryBrachistochrone: reproducibility package for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes
description:
Symbolic derivations, numerical verification scripts, figure-generation code, and manuscript sources for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes. The repository supports the companion studies of the FLRW and Vaidya sectors and of the conformal Kerr (Thakurta-Kerr) sector.

New in 1.3.0 - referee-driven release. This version answers the reproducibility findings of the Classical and Quantum Gravity review of the conformal-Kerr manuscript (CQG-116884), and every one of them was correct.

  • Restored cap_full.py. The three computer-assisted-proposition runners open with import cap_full, but the module had been factored out of the prototype during development and never archived, so a fresh clone could not run the representative certificate at all. It is restored verbatim from the prototype, with a self-test.
  • Fixed the import path in all thirteen figure generators. They inserted the repository root on sys.path while the shared style module lives one directory down, so on a fresh clone every one of them failed at import. This also exposed a silent bug in a turning-radius helper, which returned a grid point inside the forbidden region and dropped a curve from a published log-log panel with no error raised.
  • Checksums and fitted slopes are now generated, not transcribed. The same two files had carried three different SHA-256 prefixes - one printed in the manuscript, one in the previous release, one in the working tree. A single command, paper2/provenance/make_provenance.py, now runs each validation script, parses the slopes and their covariance sigmas, reads the epsilon-window out of the source, hashes every script, and emits the LaTeX macros the manuscript uses. MANIFEST.tsv maps sixteen artefacts each to one command and one checksum, and the environment lockfile - now including the computer-algebra system version - is itself a manifest entry.
  • New symbolic verification suite for the conformal-Kerr sector under paper2/verification/: 45 checks settling the local classification at the conformal stationary limit from the Hamilton equations, and 14 more certifying the exterior retrograde separatrix and its control-domain inequalities. Each check is an exact symbolic zero or a high-precision numerical convergence test, not a tolerance.

The Paper I verification suite introduced in 1.2.0 (paper1/verification/, two computer-algebra systems, exact symbolic zeros) is unchanged, as is paper1/build_paper1.sh, which makes a clean checkout turnkey.
